Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. NimbusBridge is moving fast on our search/QA pipeline and we expect inference demand to rise quickly during campaign launches. We need help sizing a Dedicated pool and defining a burst/autoscale policy that keeps costs predictable. High level:

- Current baseline: ~180 QPS across a mix of 2k and 4k token requests (mostly batching-friendly).
- Peak windows: three 2-hour campaign spikes/day where QPS can 3–4x baseline for ~6 weeks.
- Latency target: 95th <= 350ms for generation calls.

Can you share any recommended reserve sizing + burst crediting approach (how shoulder capacity and prewarm should work)? Also share an ops runbook for graceful eviction and fallback model variants in case of shortages. I attached a quick CSV with token distribution.

Goal: have a proposal by Oct 7 so procurement can review SLA language.

Best,
Samira
Director, ML Platform
NimbusBridge

Attachments: nimbusbridge-token-dist.csv (spreadsheet stub)

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial ask

Hi Samira — thanks for the details and the token histogram. Looping in Ben and Karthik for sizing/ops detail. High level we can get you a two-part deliverable: (1) a right-sized reserved slab for steady-state and (2) a burst/autoscale playbook that defines credits, prewarm strategy, and eviction ordering.

Preliminary thoughts:
- Reserve: start with a slab sized to cover 1.5x your measured baseline (so ~270 QPS equivalent) to keep steady per-token unit economics stable.
- Burst layer: a 2x shoulder pool (capacity that can be borrowed for short windows) with crediting capped per-campaign-day. Credits expire weekly to avoid long-term overcommit.
- Prewarm: prioritized prewarm for hot models 15–30 minutes before predicted campaigns, with opportunistic prewarm for lower-priority models.
- Fallbacks: recommend a quantized variant (8-bit) and a smaller context-length model for graceful degradation; automatic routing policy to fall back by latency-first policy.

Ben / Karthik — can you sketch an ops-level plan (eviction, canary on rollout, SLA constraints) and indicate what we should propose in the contract for guaranteed headroom vs. best-effort burst?

Marissa
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: marissa@redwood.com; karthik@redwood.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>; jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Oct 2029 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — ops sketch

Marissa / Karthik — draft notes from the infra POV below. I included Jordan for autoscale orchestration details.

1) Reserved slab sizing rationale   - Baseline 1.5x = 270 QPS (assumes efficient batching; we'll validate with token/process distribution).
   - Map QPS -> GPU units: using your token mix, 270 QPS ~ 12 A100-equivalent concurrent workers (estimate; exact depends on batch size and sequence length).

2) Burst / shoulder pool design   - Shoulder pool = on-demand slab of 24 GPUs (elastic) accessible as "burst credits". Credits are consumed in GPU-minutes.
   - Credit allocation: allocate a committed credit bucket per month (e.g., 200k GPU-minutes) plus campaign-day top-ups.
   - Preemption / eviction: burst workloads are preemptible; eviction order: (a) opportunistic batch jobs, (b) non-critical background queries, (c) burst callers exceeding per-tenant daily cap.

3) Autoscale policy   - Fast path (latency-critical): autoscale by workers within slab + shoulder pool up to 3x slab within policy limits; scale-up smoothing window: 30s; scale-down: 120s with cooldown.
   - Canary/fallback: new model variants first routed to 10% traffic, with automatic rollback on 5xx spike or latency regression > 20% at 95th.

4) SLA and contract language to propose   - Guaranteed steady throughput: slab-backed throughput with 99.9% uptime on core capacity.
   - Burst: best-effort with committed credit pool and a remediation credit if burst availability falls below 70% of requested GPU-minutes during a campaign window.
   - Operational runbook link (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gk-NimbusBridge-Deal (we should move the ops doc there).

Jordan — can you check if the 30s/120s windows are compatible with orchestration constraints on Dedicated? Also, we should propose a per-request token cap to prevent accidental runaway.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: ben@redwood.com; marissa@redwood.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>; karthik@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2029 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — autoscale knobs

Ben / team — confirmed: orchestration can support the suggested smoothing windows with caveats. Notes: 

- Scale-up latency: 30s is feasible for warm worker spin-up if KV cache priming is not required; for cold starts that require model page-ins and quantized kernel loads, expect 60–90s. We can mitigate via prioritized prewarm.
- Scale-down: 120s cooldown is fine; recommend preserving worker KV cache for 10 minutes when possible to reduce rewarm cost (policy toggle).
- Enforcement: we'll implement hard caps per-tenant QPS and token-length guards; we should call out a per-request token cap of 6k to protect scheduling.
- Telemetry: add per-tenant burst credit burn-rate dashboards and an alert when burn-rate > 2x baseline for more than 15 minutes.

Attached: nb-burst-policy-draft.pdf (policy boilerplate). I'll add an orchestration appendix with exact time estimates.

Jordan Blake
Product Manager, Orchestration

Hi Samira / Naveen — attaching the proposed package: capacity matrix + burst policy draft. Summary:

- Reserved slab: 12 A100-equivalent workers (~270 QPS steady).
- Burst access: up to 24 GPUs from the shoulder pool with a monthly committed credit allocation (we proposed 200k GPU-minutes) and campaign top-ups as needed.
- Autoscale controls: 30s scale-up (warm), 60–90s cold, 120s scale-down; per-tenant token cap 6k; burn-rate alerts.
- SLA: slab-backed throughput guaranteed; burst availability is best-effort with remediation credits if unmet.

Next steps:
1) Review attachments and confirm any changes to the credit envelope by Oct 10 so procurement can redline SLA language.
2) If acceptable, we'll schedule a 60-min ops handoff to your infra team (we recommend including your SREs for runbook alignment). Proposed slots: Oct 11 or Oct 12 (US PST).

Thanks — happy to walk through the policy live.
